title: Complete noob. How to make sprites?
author: Buuuni
selftext:
So i have absolute no idea on how to make good and convincing sprites for my units and enemies. I have to make around 100 total on 32x32.

How do you guys do that with ai?

comments.author: Professor_Snipe
comments.body:
Subscribe to pixellab, make, buy or generate concept art you're happy with (don't oneshot, look for issues first) and use Claude to run it through pixellab. It can animate these decently well.
If you need bigger sprites or Pixellab isn't the quality you need, take concept art, prompt the animation you need and generate a preview video with Seedance 2.5 and make sprites out of it. You need good prompts so some trial and error are going to happen naturally.

replies.author: Ill-Past4609
replies.body: Which website or sub for best bang for ur buck for seedance videos ?

replies.author: Professor_Snipe
replies.body: Dreamina was my pick in the end. You can sometimes get a freebie, though, my bank gives me a free subscription to picart for instance so I have a ton of tokens there.

replies.author: YannLeCoomer
replies.body: I'd give your AI the file and then generate some concept art that you like and then ask it how to do the rest. I've been using the API not MCP. The two do not have feature parity and there is not always a clear winner either lol. I've got Codex checking their docs every day and making notes of changes

replies.author: Ill-Past4609
replies.body: Oh wow I thought I was using the api obviously not is their a different way of installing the api then MCP :(

replies.author: YannLeCoomer
replies.body:
You don't install the API you get your key from the web UI, give it to your agent, and point it at:

[https://api.pixellab.ai/v2/openapi.json](https://api.pixellab.ai/v2/openapi.json)

Then you tell it to read it and you can either do whatever you want from there or use it with the guide I posted above

replies.author: YannLeCoomer
replies.body: It’s fine I bet you put everything we talked about into your AI and it’ll be able to answer all your questions

comments.author: alanbdee
comments.body:
I'm not sure I'm much beyond you but I did a lot of back and forth with Claude/Codex to figure out how to address it. Part of it comes from defining how things should look. AI needs a recipe to follow to create consistent sprints. One way to get consistent sprints is to actually have it create the object in 3d, then take a screenshot of it at the different angles. 

A starting point for me as well was to have AI just create the image in the way I wanted it to look. Then I let Claude create a 3d version of that. Then I was able to make small tweaks. When I tried to make small tweaks to the full ai generate sprint, it would fix one thing and ruin something else. 

I have usable sprints but nothing I'd ship today. I have been focusing more on the game part of my game. Need to make sure it's even worth trying to publish. Then I'll start diving into these services to create better sprites, textures, etc.
